Migration.Name: Add support for fractional years of useful life in FA
Migration.Comments:
https://github.com/adempiere/adempiere/issues/4412 The dictionary flip of these columns from AD_Reference_ID 11 (Integer) to 29 (Quantity) is not enough on its own: the physical columns stay numeric(10,0) and PostgreSQL rounds fractional input silently. This migration therefore widens them explicitly. Runs after SeqNo 10590, which installs the corrected altercolumn() / t_alter_column infrastructure that performs the ALTER even when no view depends on the column. t_alter_column is PostgreSQL-only, so the Oracle path uses native MODIFY. Each ALTER changes the type only: nullclause and defaultclause are SQL NULL so that the existing NOT NULL and DEFAULT 0 of the mandatory columns are preserved. Idempotent: altercolumn() compares format_type() output and skips the ALTER when the column is already unconstrained numeric.
ROLLBACK DESTROYS FRACTIONAL DATA. Narrowing numeric back to numeric(10,0) does not raise an error in PostgreSQL: it ROUNDS. Any useful life already stored as 3.3333 comes back as 3 after a rollback, silently. The RollbackStatement below is therefore only safe before fractional values are in use; once they exist, restore the fractions by hand instead of running it.

Step.Comments: Install the patched altercolumn() before touching any column, so this migration does not depend on SeqNo 10590 having run here. The previous body only issued ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE when a view depended on the column, and the fixed asset tables have none: the type change was a silent no-op, the dictionary said Quantity while the column stayed numeric(10,0), and PostgreSQL rounded 3.3333 down to 3 with no error anywhere. Body verbatim from SeqNo 10590. No RollbackStatement on purpose: restoring the older body would reintroduce that silent rounding.
Widen the useful-life year columns to unconstrained numeric so fractions persist. Type only: NOT NULL and DEFAULT are preserved.
